subject: Re: Exposure smoothing & annual cap options (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Jordan Pearson <Jordan.Pearson@beaconhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@beaconhealth.com, anna@beaconhealth.com
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA redlines: liability cap and carve-outs

Marissa — thanks for the draft MSA. Attached are Beacon's redlines (Beacon_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf). High-level ask: we need a single, predictable exposure framework for our board audit. Beacon's preference is a cumulative exposure cap tied to fees paid over the contract term (we suggested 3x fees paid, floor $500k, cap $5M) so our risk is aligned with spend.

Key carve-outs we expect to preserve: (1) willful misconduct/fraud, (2) intentional data exfiltration, (3) IP infringement claims where Redwood indemnifies, and (4) regulatory fines/penalties. We also want consequential damages to remain excluded only for third-party claims, not for breaches involving PHI/PII.

Please confirm whether Redwood is open to a fees-based cap (total-of-term) vs. an annual rolling cap. Also flag any commercial constraints — procurement timeline is tight, need a carrier-side view by next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Jordan Pearson
General Counsel, Beacon Health
(Attachment: Beacon_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Pearson <Jordan.Pearson@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: liability cap and carve-outs

Jordan — appreciate the clear redlines and the attached PDF. Quick internal note and three options we can present to Beacon as trade-off packages (we've attached a short scenarios workbook: Liability_Scenarios.xlsx):

Option A (term-based, Beacon-preferred): total cap = 3x fees paid to date (min $500k, max $5M). Pros: aligns with lifetime spend. Cons: hard to price/insure for us on long multi-year deals.

Option B (annual rolling cap): cap resets every 12 months and equals 1x annualized fees (measured by invoiced fees in prior 12 months). Pros: predictable for underwriting and our P&L. Cons: less attractive to procurement if they want a single contract-level cap.

Option C (hybrid per-incident + aggregate): per-incident cap $500k, aggregate annual cap = 1.5x annual fees, aggregate lifetime cap = 3x fees paid. Pros: balances per-event exposure and lifetime exposure. Cons: more complex to explain to finance.

On carve-outs: we are comfortable retaining carve-outs for willful misconduct, gross negligence, IP indemnity, and regulatory fines that relate to customer obligations — but we push to keep consequential damages excluded broadly except expressly for breach of confidentiality/PII/PHI and for indemnified IP claims.

Can legal weigh in on language tweaks (particularly around measurement of "fees paid" and whether the cap resets on anniversary or by invoice date)? Also, commercial input on which of these options we can live with will help prioritize redlines.

Next steps: Markus, can you draft negotiated language for each option (short bullets)? Laura, can you confirm commercial comfort range (min acceptable cap, maximum concession)? Jordan, can you share whether Beacon's board has a hard requirement for a single total-of-term cap or whether an annual structure is acceptable?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Liability_Scenarios.xlsx)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Jordan.Pearson@beaconhealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: liability cap and carve-outs — legal input

Marissa / Jordan — I'm attaching proposed redline fragments in plain text below and will turn these into tracked changes in the MSA. High-level legal positions and suggested compromise language: 

1) Measurement: define "Fees Paid" as "all amounts actually received by Redwood from Customer under Orders invoiced during the applicable measurement period, excluding taxes and third-party pass-through costs." This avoids accrual vs. cash disputes.

2) Option B (Preferred from a risk perspective): Annual rolling cap = 1.5x annual Fees Paid, where "annual" = any 12 consecutive months measured backward from the date of claim. Sample clause: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Redwood's aggregate liability for all claims arising in any 12-month period shall not exceed an amount equal to 1.5 times the Fees Paid in the 12 months preceding the first claim in such period."

3) Consequential damages carve-out: keep broad exclusion for indirect, special, incidental or consequential damages but include an explicit exception for (a) Redwood's breach of confidentiality or security obligations that caused unauthorized disclosure of PII/PHI, and (b) IP infringement indemnity where Redwood is required to indemnify. Proposed line: "Excluded Damages shall not apply to liability arising from (i) Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence, (ii) Redwood's breach of confidentiality/security obligations resulting in unauthorized disclosure of personal data, or (iii) Redwood's obligations under Section [IP Indemnity]."

4) Per-incident floors: recommend a per-incident cap floor for major incidents tied to severity tiers (e.g., Tier 1 security incident = $1M per-incident cap). If we agree to per-incident caps, require defined incident-triggered remediation credits and scope of claims that count as a single incident.

5) Insurance and payout mechanics: require notice-and-cooperation provisions and allow Redwood to offset amounts covered by insurance.

Commercial note: legal can accept a 1x annual Fees Paid cap as long as it's paired with (i) stronger carve-outs for indemnities, (ii) per-incident maxima for security events, and (iii) a mutual SLA credits schedule. If sales needs a lower number for negotiation (1x), document that as fallback.

I'll prepare tracked changes for Option B and the hybrid and circulate by EOD tomorrow.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan.Pearson@beaconhealth.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: commercial constraints and negotiation stance

Team — pragmatic commercial view from Sales: Beacon is strategic in the Midwest health vertical; losing them over cap structure would slow ARR growth. Practical negotiating posture: lead with Option B (annual rolling cap) at 1.0x annual Fees Paid, but include a fallback to 1.5x with the legal carve-outs Markus requested. If Beacon insists on a single term cap, we can offer a capped total-of-term at 2.0x fees paid (not 3x) with a $1M per-incident cap for security events and an explicit list of carve-outs.

Additional asks for Beacon: (a) commitment to a 36-month initial term and (b) minimum annual spend guarantee of $400k — those commercial concessions materially reduce our exposure and should be part of any concession on cap.

Suggested negotiation script: 
- Offer #1 (preferred): Annual rolling cap = 1.0x Fees Paid; carve-outs per Markus; SLA credits and incident remediation protocol; 36-month minimum term.
- Offer #2 (fallback): Annual rolling cap = 1.5x Fees Paid; same carve-outs; $1M per-incident cap; 24-month term.
- Offer #3 (only if procurement insists on total-of-term): Total cap = max($1M, 2.0x Fees Paid, not to exceed $4M) with carve-outs and per-incident floors.

Marissa: if legal can produce redline language that maps to Offer #1 quickly, I'll push Beacon procurement to accept.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Pearson <Jordan.Pearson@beaconhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@beaconhealth.com, anna@beaconhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-04T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exposure smoothing & annual cap options (MSA + Order Form) — Beacon preference

Marissa / Team — thanks for the clear options and quick turn. Beacon discussed this with finance and the board. We prefer an annual rolling cap structure (your Offer #1) because it provides predictable budgeting and avoids a large lump-sum exposure that complicates our audit forecasts. Beacon is willing to accept an annual cap equal to 1.0x Fees Paid (measured by prior 12 months invoiced), provided Redwood accepts the following: (1) explicit carve-out for regulatory fines arising directly from Redwood's processing of Beacon data, (2) consequential damages remain excluded except for breaches involving PII/PHI or indemnified IP claims, and (3) per-incident security cap set at $750k for Tier 1.

If you can circulate a final redline (tracked) and an updated Order Form (OrderForm_Draft.xlsx) with those parameters, procurement will route for signature. Please also include a DocuSign link when ready.

Jordan Pearson
General Counsel, Beacon Health
(Attachment: OrderForm_Draft.xlsx)
